crime_highlights: The child was determined to have died from pneumonia brought on by the aspiration of vomit
his body was found to be covered with bruises, abrasions, and scrapes
assaults over a period of weeks, failure to provide proper nourishment and care, and the refusal and neglect of the appellants to seek help when his condition became serious
A physician who examined the younger child, Raymond George, noted that he also had significant injuries on his body, some being fresh and some being weeks old
rationale_highlights: the learned sentencing judge failed to give sufficient weight to the systemic background factors that led to these offenders appearing before the court on the charges that they faced
Both of the appellants came from backgrounds that were gravely disadvantaged
I consider the sentences imposed were too high

pre-Gladue cases involving aboriginal offenders should now be assessed in light of the principles enunciated in Gladue which urge courts to take greater account of the systemic factors that may contribute to aboriginal offenders being in conflict with the law
